chunk_findings.detail:
In `glob_clashes`, when one live lease overlaps the current item on more than one glob, the loop still appends only `pairs[0]` for that item:
```python
pairs = conflicts(globs, lease.globs, shared)
if pairs:
    out.append(Clash(other_id, pairs[0], lease))
```
So for current globs `["brief.py", "lane_views.py"]` held by another lease, `glob_clashes` returns one `Clash`, not two, even though both globs conflict. Any refusal report built from this list will still omit `lane_views.py`; the original "one overlap per refusal" bug persists when a single holder holds multiple requested files.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/admission.py:glob_clashes

chunk_findings.detail:
Both queued-behind refusals now print `ahead.globs`, but `ahead` is the queued lease ahead of the refused item, so `.globs` is the whole set of globs the ahead item asked for, not the globs of the refused item that are queued behind it. Input: the refused item asks for `brief.py`; the ahead lease holds `brief.py`, `lane_views.py`, and `reporting.py`. The new message says:
`those files (brief.py, lane_views.py, reporting.py) are queued behind ...`
even though only `brief.py` is the refused item's conflicting file. The message should list the refused item's conflicting globs (or the intersection with its current request), not the full `ahead.globs`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/reservations.py:201, ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim_guard_queued.py:25

chunk_findings.detail: `clash_report` returns `[oid for oid, _lz, _p in clashes]` without deduplicating item IDs. `glob_clashes` represents one entry per overlapping `(mine, theirs)` pair, so a single conflicting lease holding two globs overlapped by the claim yields two entries for the same item, e.g. `("B", lease_B, ("src/a.py","src/a.py"))` and `("B", lease_B, ("src/b.py","src/b.py"))` produce `_ids == ["B", "B"]`. The docstring says this is the list of "every conflicting item id ... a waiter must wait on each"; any caller that uses it to append `lease.waiting` entries will enqueue the same item twice. The added test only covers two distinct item IDs, so it does not catch this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/common.py:clash_report

chunk_findings.detail: The test only checks that both glob strings and both holder strings appear in `main`; it never checks that each holder is attached to the correct glob. A wrong implementation that emitted `src/a.py ... held by agent-holder2` and `src/b.py ... held by HOLDER` would still pass. Since the promise being fixed is specifically to list every conflicting glob *with its holder*, the association is the core behavior and should be asserted.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_wait_claim_agree.py:test_claim_refusal_lists_every_conflicting_holder

chunk_findings.detail: `glob_clashes` still keeps only `pairs[0]` per other item (`out.append(Clash(other_id, pairs[0], lease))` and the offered-path twin). A clash record has one pair and no claim-glob list, and `clash_report` is only given those clashes, so the dropped pairs cannot be rebuilt. Input: one live lease held by `sw-cedefaults` on `brief.py`, `lane_views.py`, and `reporting.py`, claim globs that overlap all three. `conflicts()` returns three pairs; the refusal built from this list still names a single glob, which is the failure this change says it fixes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/admission.py:glob_clashes

chunk_findings.detail: `clash_report` always renders `held by {lz.holder}` and has no queue-place branch. Given a clash whose lease is only queued — the case the bug cites for `update --globs` (`those globs are queued behind sw-cedefaults`) — the text is `'src/a.py' overlaps 'src/**' held by sw-cedefaults on Y`, which claims a hold that does not exist and never states queue place.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/common.py:clash_report

chunk_findings.detail: The regression only claims two live holders and checks that both paths and both agent ids appear as substrings before `Recorded:`. It never runs `update --globs` against a queued lease, and a refusal that merely echoes Y's own glob list plus both agent names (without pairing each glob to its holder or queue place) satisfies the asserts, so the stated bug can remain and the test still passes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_wait_claim_agree.py:test_claim_refusal_lists_every_conflicting_holder

data.summary: The harness channel code exists (ask -> question -> attest reading Kilo SQLite + typed digest; r-approval-chat-channel; dx-approvals-kilo-harness done), but the auto-attest loop is missing: after the operator answers the Kilo question tool no agent runs attest, and the surfaced question text is not the canonical ask payload so scan_kilo does not match, so ddflow stays pending and the operator is asked to run terminal approve --all. Fix: auto-attest pending approvals after the operator answers (surface the canonical ask text, then attest), so a chat answer alone approves with no terminal/SSH.

evidence.note: Claim: a FINDING block whose location is prose (not path:line/path:symbol) or whose paragraph is unfinished reasoning with no defect is stored as a normal MEDIUM finding and blocks the gate. Mechanism: parse() in ddflow/services/review/engine.py accepts any location string and any paragraph; blocking_findings() counts every finding. Refutation: a finding with location 'leaving.py:257? The line in _leave ...' and detail 'We need cite line number' would NOT be marked malformed and would still block. Cheap test (ran FIRST, on unfixed code): python -m pytest tests/test_review_finding_unfinished_reasoning.py -x -q -> FAILED AttributeError 'Finding' object has no attribute 'malformed'. After fix the same test passes (8 passed) and blocking_findings([f],...) == [] for malformed. VERDICT CONFIRMED.

Relevant standing rules consulted and honored: r-derive-dont-store (malformed flag derived from location/detail at parse, nothing stored separately), r-evidence-over-assertion (regression test first), r-fail-closed tempered by B-review-finding-empty-text precedent (malformed marked not dropped, still recorded). No file-specific rules overridden.

Fix implemented and committed 3aa9e0f04: parse() marks malformed findings; blocking_findings() excludes them; _untriaged() skips them; evidence records the malformed flag. Regression test tests/test_review_finding_unfinished_reasoning.py (5 tests) added.

chunk_findings.detail: The citation pattern rejects pytest-style `path::symbol` locations even though the comment on `_CITATION_RE` says those nodes are included. `[^\s:?;]+` cannot consume `:`, and `(?::?{_SYMBOL}|:\d+...)` cannot match a second colon, so `_CITATION_RE.match("tests/test_review.py::test_parse")` is None. A real finding `FINDING HIGH tests/test_review.py::test_parse` / `the parser drops the last finding` is therefore given `malformed="location is prose, not a path:line or path:symbol"`, and `blocking_findings` returns `[]`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/engine.py:_CITATION_RE

chunk_findings.detail: The second signal does not match the stated rule that a paragraph stating no defect is malformed on its own. It fires only when `_META_REASONS` hits (`cite line`, `let me`, `i'll`, `note to self`). Given location `ddflow/api/lifecycle/leaving.py:257` and detail `We should think about whether this is correct and then write it up later`, both regexes miss, `_malformed_reason` returns `""`, and the unfinished paragraph still blocks the gate. The same word list also drops a real defect that uses a meta phrase but not a listed defect word: `Note to self: this path drops the result on timeout` is marked malformed because `drops` is not in `_DEFECT_WORDS`.

chunk_findings.detail: `_DEFECT_WORDS` short-circuits the mid-sentence check, so unfinished reasoning that happens to contain a listed word is still a blocking finding. Given location `ddflow/api/lifecycle/leaving.py:257` and detail `I never finished this thought about the leave path`, `_DEFECT_WORDS` matches `never`, `_unfinished_reasoning` returns False, `_malformed_reason` returns `""`, and the gate still counts it. chunk_findings.detail: A paragraph is treated as a finished sentence whenever the last non-space character is `.`, so the usual mid-thought ellipsis does not count as unfinished. Given a valid citation `ddflow/api/lifecycle/leaving.py:257` and detail `We need cite line number and then see whether the call...`, `_TERMINATOR` matches the final `.` of `...`, no defect word is required, and the reasoning is stored as a real finding and blocks the gate.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression that is supposed to fail on unfixed code still feeds the parser the old meta phrase "We need cite line number" on a clean `path:line`. That string was already in the previous `_META_REASONS` list, so `_malformed_reason` marked it malformed before this change and the test would pass on the unfixed engine. The input the confirmed review showed slipping through — location `ddflow/api/lifecycle/leaving.py:257` and detail `We should think about whether this is correct and then write it up later` (no defect named, sentence never closed, no "cite line"/"let me" hit) — is not asserted. A parser that only still special-cases those meta words therefore satisfies this suite and still stores that paragraph as a blocking MEDIUM finding.

evidence.note: roborev reviewed the branch diff iteratively (jobs 4549-4553, reviewer elmdeepseekpro/[REDACTED:name] via kilo). Every finding applied, then re-reviewed and re-fixed until convergence: prose-location classifier narrowed to whitespace+?/ellipsis (path:257? and ;-separated and multi-spot citations kept), malformed findings excluded from blocking_findings+_untriaged, surfaced in the triage listing as 'malformed' and in a malformed_findings pass key, carried through merge_rerun, Finding.malformed doc aligned. Final code ruff-clean; 37 focused review tests pass. Remaining 'two-spot citation with a trailing ?' is THEORETICAL and roborev itself flagged it not-actionable without a concrete repo citation form.

chunk_findings.detail: The gate still counts the class of unfinished-reasoning findings the bug requires to be dropped. `_malformed_reason` returns a reason only when the location has both whitespace and `?`/`...`; any other non-citation is stored as a normal finding and still blocks. Given location `We need cite line number` and detail `We need cite line number and continues as the model thinking aloud, ending mid-sentence` with severity MEDIUM, the function returns `""`, `parse` sets `malformed=""`, and `records`/`_blocking_findings` treat it as a real below-floor or blocking finding. The same miss happens for a valid citation whose text is reasoning with no failure (`location=ddflow/api/lifecycle/leaving.py:257`, detail starting `We need cite line number` and ending mid-sentence): expected behavior is drop or mark malformed on either condition, and this path still fails the gate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/engine.py:_malformed_reason

chunk_findings.detail: A real defect is dropped whenever the location string also contains whitespace and `?` or an ellipsis, because malformed findings are removed before severity ranking. Given a HIGH finding with location `auth.py:42 is the token check skipped?` and detail `given an empty token, line 42 returns allow, which is wrong`, `_malformed_reason` returns a reason, the filter `findings = [f for f in findings if not getattr(f, "malformed", "")]` removes it, and the round can pass with no blocking finding. The comment that a finding naming a real spot is never silently dropped is false for that input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/model.py:_blocking_findings

chunk_findings.detail: The bug requires a finding to be dropped or marked malformed when its location is not a citation or when its text is unfinished reasoning with no failure stated. `test_reasoning_on_a_clean_citation_is_kept_not_dropped` locks the opposite: input `FINDING MEDIUM ddflow/api/lifecycle/leaving.py:257` plus `We need to cite a line number and then decide.` is asserted `not f.malformed`, so that block still counts as a normal finding and still fails the gate via `blocking_findings`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_finding_unfinished_reasoning.py:88

chunk_findings.detail: A location is treated as non-blocking only when it has both whitespace and `?` or an ellipsis. That misses the stated gate rule: a location that is not `path:line` or `path:symbol` must not count. Given location `We need cite line number of the defect in _leave`, `_malformed_reason` returns `""` because there is no prose mark, `parse` stores `malformed=""`, and the finding still blocks. The same hole applies to a valid citation whose detail is unfinished reasoning with no failure (`leaving.py:257` plus `We need cite line number` ending mid-sentence): the text half of B-review-finding-is-unfinished-reasoning is never applied.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/engine.py:_malformed_reason

chunk_findings.detail: The same predicate drops a real defect whenever the location field is the bug's shape plus a stated failure. data.probe: Not a defect: the deterministic location signal requires BOTH whitespace and a prose mark (?/ellipsis) precisely because whitespace alone is a multi-spot or annotated citation (roborev 4550/4553: 'foo.py:10 bar.py:20', 'a.py:12; b.py:34'). Marking 'We need cite line number...' (whitespace, no mark) malformed needs the semantic 'states a defect' test, which this review's own #2 is the opposite direction of: no deterministic rule satisfies both. The location-with-mark rule is the documented fix.

data.probe: This and #1 are the same irreducible ambiguity in opposite directions: #1 asks to mark MORE prose malformed, #2 asks to mark LESS. Distinguishing 'path:line? + reasoning' (the reported finding, must drop) from 'path:line? + stated defect' (must keep) is deciding whether the prose states a defect -- a semantic property no deterministic rule decides both ways (this review's earlier 'returns the location string' was such a false drop). The shipped fix implements the deterministic bug-spec'd signal (location not a citation -> reasoning) and is fail-closed on the paragraph; the other direction is the documented out-of-scope text signal.

chunk_findings.detail: A location is treated as non-blocking only when it has both whitespace and `?` or an ellipsis. That misses the stated gate rule: a location that is not `path:line` or `path:symbol` must not count. Given location `We need cite line number of the defect in _leave`, `_malformed_reason` returns `""` because there is no prose mark, `parse` stores `malformed=""`, and the finding still blocks. The same hole applies to a valid citation whose detail is unfinished reasoning with no failure (`leaving.py:257` plus `We need cite line number` ending mid-sentence): the text half of B-review-finding-is-unfinished-reasoning is never applied.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review/engine.py:_malformed_reason

chunk_findings.detail: The same predicate drops a real defect whenever the location field is the bug's shape plus a stated failure. Given location `ddflow/api/lifecycle/leaving.py:257? given input X, line 257 returns None, which is wrong because the empty case is unhandled`, `_malformed_reason` returns `location is prose, not a path:line or path:symbol`. `parse` sets `malformed`, and both `model` blocking filter and the `records.py` `if malformed: return "passed"` path exclude it from the gate, so a review that stated a concrete failure passes.
